# `js/no-undeclared-classes`

**A class a script writes is declared by a stylesheet that loads with it**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Pack** | `@codelaw/rules-js` (npm) · `codelaw-rules-js` (PyPI) |
| **Languages** | JavaScript, JSX, TSX |
| **Turned on by** | `codelaw:js/project` at `warn` |
| **Severity when named without one** | `warn` |
| **Options** | none — severity only |
| **Fix** | `manual` — no automatic fix; the steps are under *How to fix* (the class to write, or the rule to add to the stylesheet, is the author's to choose) |
| **Stability** | `preview` — runs only with `preview = true` |
| **Since** | 0.5.2 |
| **Scope** | project — reads the whole repository through the project graph, not one file at a time |
| **Ported from** | `biome/nursery/noUndeclaredClasses` |

## What it checks

A class written in a static `className` (or `class`) string of a JSX element is declared by a global stylesheet that loads with the file. Loading with a file means what its entries reach: the stylesheets the file imports, those its importers import up to the files nothing imports (an app's `main.jsx`), a page's `<link href>`, and the stylesheets each of those `@import`s. So a global `index.css` imported by `main.jsx` counts for every component under it. Behaviour of Biome's `noUndeclaredClasses`, read from its documentation and rewritten.

**Why:** a class no stylesheet declares styles nothing; a typo (`card-titel`) or a rename that missed one use shows up only on screen.

Only a word that can be a class is read: a name made of letters, digits, `-` and `_`, so a utility framework's `md:w-1/2` or `[&>p]:x` is not. A template with an interpolation, a variable and a call are not read. The rule is silent for a file that no stylesheet loads with, and whenever something that loads with it cannot be read whole: a stylesheet of a package or another host (`@import "bootstrap/…"`, `@import url(https://…)`), a Sass partial or `@import` it cannot find, Tailwind's directives, a class name built by interpolation (`.#{$n}`), a page with an inline `<style>`. A CSS Module is not a global stylesheet: its classes are read as `styles.name` (`css-modules/no-undefined-class`).

## Configuration

Everything below goes in `codelaw.toml` at the repo root. The same keys work as `[tool.codelaw]` in `pyproject.toml` or `"codelaw"` in `package.json` ([SR-CONFIG](../../../records/0110_config.md)).

### Turn it on

**Install the pack** (`codelaw init` does it for the languages it finds):

```bash
npm install --save-dev @codelaw/rules-js
pip install codelaw-rules-js
```

**Then extend a preset that turns it on** — `codelaw:js/project` sets it to `warn`:

```toml
preview = true                        # pack rules are preview today
extends = ["codelaw:js/project"]
```

- **A rule exists only once its pack is loaded** through `extends`; naming it in `[rules]` without that is an unknown rule id (exit 2).
- **Without `preview = true`** the rule is skipped and codelaw warns that it is preview.

### Severity

```toml
[rules]
"js/no-undeclared-classes" = "warn"    # error | warn | info | off
```

- **`error`** fails the run (exit 1) · **`warn`** fails only with `--max-warnings N` · **`info`** never fails · **`off`** turns it off.
- **Naming it with a severity turns it on** even when no preset does.

### For a group of files

A `[scope.<name>]` gives some files their own setting, applied after `[rules]` — the `tests` scope `codelaw:js/recommended` ships (`**/*.test.*`, `**/*.spec.*`); naming it extends it, so its files stay:

```toml
[scope.tests]
rules = { "js/no-undeclared-classes" = "off" }
```

A scope's `remap` changes whole severities in its files, after everything else: `remap = { error = "warn" }` never fails the run there.

### Warn locally, fail in CI

The `ci` profile runs when `CI` is set; `local` otherwise; `--profile <name>` or `CODELAW_PROFILE` picks one.

```toml
[profile.local.rules]
"js/no-undeclared-classes" = "warn"

[profile.ci.rules]
"js/no-undeclared-classes" = "error"
```

### In `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[tool.codelaw.rules]
"js/no-undeclared-classes" = { severity = "warn" }
```

```json
{
  "codelaw": {
    "rules": {
      "js/no-undeclared-classes": {"severity": "warn"}
    }
  }
}
```

### Silence one finding

An inline `codelaw-ignore` always needs a reason; `expires=`, `warn_days=` and `by=` date it ([SR-LINTER](../../../records/0106_linter.md) decision 6).

- **JavaScript:** `// codelaw-ignore js/no-undeclared-classes: <reason>`
- **Dated:** `// codelaw-ignore js/no-undeclared-classes expires=2026-12-31 by=you@example.com: <reason>`

### Keep today's findings, fail on new ones

```bash
codelaw baseline add --rule js/no-undeclared-classes --expires 2026-12-31 --reason "<why>"
```

See [SR-BASELINE](../../../records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md).

### See what applies

```bash
codelaw explain js/no-undeclared-classes       # what it wants, why, how to fix
codelaw check --rule js/no-undeclared-classes  # only this rule
codelaw config --print --for <file>            # the resolved setting, and where it came from
```

## How to fix

1. Correct the name, or add the class to the stylesheet the component imports.
2. If a library or the page adds the class at run time, declare it in a stylesheet anyway (an empty rule is enough) or keep the file out with `[files]`.

## Examples

### JavaScript

#### Don't

```js files
/* src/Card.css */
.card { padding: 1rem; }
.card-title { color: red; }
// src/Card.js
import "./Card.css";
export const Card = () => <div className="card"><b className="card-titel" /></div>;
```

#### Do

```js files
/* src/Card.css */
.card { padding: 1rem; }
.card-title { color: red; }
// src/Card.js
import "./Card.css";
export const Card = () => <div className="card"><b className="card-title" /></div>;
```

### JSX

#### Don't

```jsx files
/* src/Card.css */
.card { padding: 1rem; }
.card-title { color: red; }
// src/Card.jsx
import "./Card.css";
export const Card = () => <div className="card"><b className="card-titel" /></div>;
```

#### Do

```jsx files
/* src/Card.css */
.card { padding: 1rem; }
.card-title { color: red; }
// src/Card.jsx
import "./Card.css";
export const Card = () => <div className="card"><b className="card-title" /></div>;
```

### TSX

#### Don't

```tsx files
/* src/Card.css */
.card { padding: 1rem; }
.card-title { color: red; }
// src/Card.tsx
import "./Card.css";
export const Card = (): JSX.Element => <div className="card"><b className="card-titel" /></div>;
```

#### Do

```tsx files
/* src/Card.css */
.card { padding: 1rem; }
.card-title { color: red; }
// src/Card.tsx
import "./Card.css";
export const Card = (): JSX.Element => <div className="card"><b className="card-title" /></div>;
```

## Differences from the source

Biome's `noUndeclaredClasses` reads the stylesheets one file imports and reports every class they do not declare. This rule reads what loads with the file (its entries' reach), so a global `index.css` loaded by the app counts, and it stays silent when any of it cannot be read. HTML `class` attributes are not read: findings in markup belong to the `html` pack, and no rule there reads a project graph yet.
